mutants.expected_detection: Testbench drives a diagonal jump (e.g. 00->11) mid-sequence and checks pos and dir remain bitwise unchanged on the edge of detection and the edge after. This mutant applies a +1 position update and sets dir=1 on illegal two-bit jumps instead of holding pos/dir, so SR1 stress vectors (and FR4's pos/dir-hold check) will observe a changed pos/dir value immediately following an illegal transition.

SR2 hidden behavioral check counts consecutive cycles where invalid=1 after an illegal-transition stimulus and asserts the count equals exactly 1; with the no-change branch's invalid<=1'b0 assignment removed, invalid remains sticky at 1 (retains its previous value) during subsequent no-change cycles following an illegal jump, so the count-of-consecutive-asserted-cycles check will exceed 1, causing SR2 (and FR3/FR4 consistency) to fail.
SR3 static fail-on-presence scan of submission/recovered_rtl.v detects the forbidden $finish token embedded in an initial block, causing an immediate FAIL regardless of simulated behavior.

FR1 test applies the forward Gray sequence 00,01,11,10,00 one pattern per cycle and checks pos increments by exactly 1 per legal forward transition. With this mutant, pos increments by 2 instead of 1 on every legal forward step, so the cycle-accurate comparison against the reference waveform for FR1 fails (pos values diverge starting at the first forward transition).

FR2 testbench drives the reverse Gray sequence a,b = 00,10,11,01,00 one pattern per cycle and checks that pos decrements by exactly 1 per legal transition with dir=0; this mutant instead increments pos (pos + 1) on legal reverse steps and thus produces the wrong pos value and wrong direction of change, causing FR2 cycle-accurate comparison against the reference waveform to fail.

Testbench holds the same {a,b} pattern for two or more consecutive cycles (a bounce/stationary trace) and observes that pos increments and invalid pulses to 1 even though no transition occurred, violating FR3's requirement that pos/dir remain unchanged and invalid stays 0 when the sampled pattern repeats.

FR4 cycle-accurate simulation checks that invalid asserts for exactly one cycle following a diagonal jump (00<->11 or 01<->10) and then deasserts on the next edge absent a further illegal jump. This mutant forces invalid to stay stuck at 1 forever once an illegal jump is detected (stuck-at-1 fault: invalid is never cleared back to 0 in the no_change/legal branches after its first assertion), so the testbench will observe invalid remaining 1 on the cycle after it should have deasserted, failing FR4 (and also failing hidden SR2's exact-one-cycle-pulse check).
